item.title: Fed's Williams says US economy remains resilient, appropriate time to gather more information
item.description:
• US economy remarkably resilient
  • Growth has strengthened
  • US facing unusual supply and demand shocks
  • Remarkably stable and solid labour market
  • We've seen tariffs effect work way through, mostly behind us
  • Energy passing through to inflation as expected
  • Inflation expectations well anchored
  • Wage growth consistent with 2% goal
  • This is appropriate time to gather more info

New York Fed President John Williams highlighted the resilience of the US economy while signalling that the Federal Reserve can afford to take time to assess incoming data before making further policy decisions.

Williams said economic growth has strengthened, describing the US economy as remarkably resilient despite facing unusual demand and supply-side shocks. He also characterised the labour market as remarkably stable and solid, suggesting that employment conditions remain broadly supportive of the economic outlook.

On inflation, Williams noted that the impact of tariffs has largely worked its way through the economy and is now mostly behind us. Meanwhile, energy costs are passing through to inflation broadly as expected. He added that longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored and wage growth is consistent with the Fed's 2% inflation target.

Williams is relatively comfortable with the current economic backdrop and doesn't see the need to rush on interest rates.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: A welcome change for gold as tech selloff fails to spark heavy liquidation, breaking the recent pattern
item.description:
Gold came under some pressure yesterday amid the tech stocks rout. The good news is that we haven’t experienced the same strong liquidation that we’ve seen in the past weeks.

This might be due to the change in context and positioning. We now have a Democratic Congress which is going to restrain fiscal expansion and likely limit the rise in Treasury yields. At the same time, we still have the war in Iran that is likely to keep inflation expectations high.

The result is lower real yields, especially with the rout in tech stocks weighing on growth expectations and nominal yields.

The positioning in gold is also much less crowded than at the start of the year. BofA's FMS survey had already shown in July that gold was the most undervalued since 2023, which should provide further support for the precious metal.

The focus will now be on the US-Iran situation and the Fed. If Trump decides to escalate the war, inflation expectations would rise alongside weakening growth outlook, creating a stagflationary environment. This is bullish for gold.

At the same time, if we get a de-escalation, we could see a dovish repricing on easing inflation concerns, which could also support gold in the short-term.

Today, we have the US NFP report. Soft data could lower rate hike probabilities further and trigger a rally in gold. A hot report, on the other hand, is unlikely to change much for the Fed, so a downward spike could be quickly faded.

 

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that gold(CFD contract) broke above the key downward trendline and pulled back to retest it. The buyers will likely continue to pile in around these levels, with a defined risk below the trendline, to keep targeting new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will need to see the price breaking below the major upward trendline to open the door for new lows.

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, we can see that the minor support around the 4,080 level didn’t hold but the price still bounced from the broken trendline. The buyers will likely want to see the price rising back above the broken support zone to pile in for a rally into the 4,500 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will need the price to fall back below the trendline to extend the pullback into the minor upward trendline around the 3,960 level next.

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining yesterday’s pullback. The sellers will likely lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the upward trendline. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 4,500 level next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

UPCOMING CATALYSTS

Todaywe conclude the week with the US NFP report and the University of Michigan Consumer sentiment survey.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Newmont stock breaks out of a two-month downtrend. But buyers have a test to pass.
item.description:
Gold and other precious metals are showing signs of a potentially significant bullish reversal.

But not every investor wants to trade physical gold, futures or other metal-linked instruments.

One stock worth watching is Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM), a major gold producer. Its four-hour chart shows a promising technical development, although the most useful part of this analysis is not a prediction. It's the price map that can help us assess whether the breakout succeeds or fails.

I'm not recommending that readers buy Newmont. Technical patterns can fail, and even a strong rally in gold does not guarantee that gold-mining shares will follow.

A downtrend that may have turned into a bull flag

As discussed in investingLive's recent gold technical analysis, gold has broken above an important declining trendline, raising the possibility of a broader recovery.

Newmont's four-hour chart presents an interesting parallel.

Since early September, NEM has traded inside a descending channel, repeatedly making lower highs and generally struggling to maintain rallies.

But after declining toward $104.50 in late October, the stock recovered sharply, breaking above the channel's upper boundary and advancing toward $122-$123.

That changes the technical interpretation.

What previously looked like a persistent downtrend may prove to have been a bull flag, a downward-sloping consolidation that can interrupt a larger bullish move before the advance resumes.

The important distinction is that a breakout does not guarantee the pattern will work. Buyers still need to demonstrate that they can defend the recovery.

Why $117-$118 may be the most interesting area on the chart

The chart reveals something particularly useful.

Newmont has pulled back toward the $117-$118 area, which coincides with the Point of Control (PoC) of the recent trading range.

For readers unfamiliar with the term, the Point of Control represents the price level where the greatest amount of volume was traded over a selected period.

It can become an important reference point because considerable trading activity previously occurred there. However, that does not automatically make it support.

For Newmont, the question is whether the recent breakout has changed market behavior sufficiently for buyers to defend this area.

A successful retest could strengthen the bullish interpretation. A sustained move below it would indicate that the recovery is losing momentum.

The stock also faces resistance around $120, making the nearby price structure particularly interesting.

The Newmont stock price map: What would strengthen or weaken the bullish case?

Rather than assuming that the breakout means Newmont is heading higher, I would focus on three possible developments.

1. Bullish continuation: Above $120, then $122-$123

If NEM establishes sustained trading above $120 and subsequently clears the $122-$123 resistance area, the bullish case would improve.

That could bring the September high around $130.75 back into focus.

It would not guarantee a move toward that level, but it would indicate that buyers have overcome another important obstacle.

2. Constructive pullback: Holding $117-$118

A pullback that stabilizes around $117-$118, particularly if followed by a higher low and renewed buying, could provide evidence that the recent breakout is holding.

This would be constructive even without an immediate rally.

In fact, watching how a market behaves after an initial breakout can sometimes be more informative than watching the breakout itself.

3. Failed breakout: Below approximately $115

Sustained trading below $115 would materially weaken the emerging bullish structure.

Attention could then shift toward the $112 support area. Further deterioration could eventually put the November low around $104.50 back into focus.

That would suggest the apparent bull flag breakout had failed, rather than developed into a sustained bullish continuation.

Gold exposure through a stock is different from owning gold

There is another important distinction for investors.

Newmont is a mining company, not a direct substitute for bullion. Its share price reflects gold prices, but also production volumes, operating costs, capital spending and broader equity-market conditions.

In its third-quarter 2026 results, Newmont reported approximately 1.3 million attributable ounces of gold production and $1.9 billion in free cash flow. The company also maintained its full-year production outlook while improving its full-year cost guidance.

Those fundamentals may matter to investors assessing the company beyond the chart, but they do not eliminate mining-specific risks.

A recovering gold price can benefit producers, yet Newmont shares can still underperform if costs rise, production disappoints or equity markets come under pressure.

The lesson: A good map is more valuable than a confident prediction

What interests me most about Newmont is not simply that it has broken above a descending channel.

It's that the chart now provides several identifiable reference areas against which we can evaluate the bullish hypothesis.

The $117-$118 area may help reveal whether buyers are defending the breakout. A recovery above $120 and $122-$123 would strengthen the continuation case. A sustained decline below $115 would challenge it.

We don't need to know in advance which outcome will occur to make the analysis useful.

For investors exploring possible exposure to a precious-metals recovery through listed companies, Newmont is an interesting stock to investigate further.

But a potential bull flag is not a reason to buy automatically. Its value lies in understanding what would confirm the opportunity, what would undermine it and when patience may be the better decision.

What else is interesting for traders and investors today?

Following a punishing tech rout that saw Nasdaq-100 futures plunge 5,250 points (Almost 17%...!) from their October high, I am tracking whether buyers can turn an initial 800-point bounce off historical support into something more durable. As I broke down in my Nasdaq technical analysis after yesterday's crash, the 26,350–26,400 zone provided an immediate reaction, but my tradeCompass framework demands sustained trading above 27,200 to validate a constructive bullish continuation, otherwise, slipping below 26,850 risks reopening downside exposure.

This fragile stabilization comes as regional bourses absorb heavy selling, detailed in the investingLive Asia-Pacific news wrap on global tech rout growth concerns, where heavy pressure on chip and data-center supply chains spilled across Asian equity sessions.

Macro and geopolitical crosscurrents continue to dictate intraday positioning, with Adam Button at investingLive.com noting that the market is waiting for critical policy signals from Donald Trump regarding post-midterm tariff strategy and Middle East tensions, leaving risk assets caught between relief rallies and supply-side uncertainties.

Traders now turn their focus to high-impact economic catalysts to close out the week; as Giuseppe Dellamotta outlined when previewing the main economic events on today's calendar, session volatility is poised to spike with the release of the U.S. non-farm payrolls (NFP) report, Canadian employment data, and the preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey.

Educational market analysis only. Not a recommendation to buy or sell. Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: investingLive Asia-pacific news wrap: Global tech stocks rout raises growth concerns
item.description:
US Democrats are reportedly targeting President Trump's tariffs on Canada as the first step towards rolling back parts of his administration's trade policy. Senator Wyden said there is overwhelming support for repealing tariffs on Canadian products. Meanwhile, BoC Governor Macklem said he remains optimistic about lower US tariffs but cannot rule out further escalation before trade conditions improve.

President Trump, in a Truth Social post, acknowledged the sharp equity market sell-off, saying stocks had suffered one of their worst days ever but would ultimately become bigger and stronger.

War Secretary Hegseth could reportedly face an impeachment vote as soon as next week. Secretary of State Rubio denied reports that he was considering leaving the administration, saying he intended to remain until the end of Trump's term.

Texas Governor-elect said data centre development should be halted until measures are introduced to protect residents.

The US-Iran situation remained mostly unchanged, with President Trump saying Washington needed to decide whether to take further action against Tehran, while adding that he would prefer not to destroy the rest of Iran.

According to Axios, Trump met with his national security team before making the comments, while CENTCOM is reportedly finalising preparations for potentially resuming major combat operations. However, no new directive has been issued.

Diplomatic efforts continue. Iran reportedly submitted a new nuclear proposal to the US through Qatar, but a senior Iranian official said Tehran would only discuss it once Washington meets its seven demands. Fars News also reported that Iran does not envisage further diplomatic steps until those conditions are met.

The NYT reported that Iran is reviewing concrete proposals from mediators concerning its nuclear programme, with Vice President Vance reportedly emerging as a key supporter of Qatar-led mediation efforts.

Nevertheless, US military strikes remain an option, with reports suggesting Trump could consider limited strikes against Iranian nuclear facilities rather than broader attacks on energy infrastructure.

Asian governments signalled their readiness to respond to heightened financial market volatility following the global equity sell-off. South Korea's finance minister said authorities would take necessary measures to prevent excessive market reactions and significant deviations from fundamentals. The government also announced a three-month easing of margin requirements.

Taiwan ordered regulators to closely monitor equity markets and prepare flexible stabilisation measures. Meanwhile, Japanese PM Takaichi said the government was considering support payments for more than 30% of workers.

In Canada, the government proposed total borrowing of CAD 611bln for 2027/28, up from CAD 587bln in 2026/27. However, deficit projections were revised lower across the forecast horizon. The government also lowered its GDP growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027.

Looking ahead, the focus will remain on the fallout from the US midterm elections and the developments in the US-Iran war. 

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

What are FX option expiries?

The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts.

When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET).

Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on).

As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: What are the main events for today?
item.description:
EUROPEAN SESSION

In the European session, we don't have much on the agenda other that a couple of low-tier releases like the Swiss consumer confidence and the Eurozone retail sales. The data won't change anything for the respective central banks, so the market reaction will be muted. 

The focus remains on the fallout from the US midterm elections and the US-Iran situation. The rout in tech stocks has weighed on growth expectations, putting pressure on Treasury yields and rate hike expectations. The probabilities for a December Fed rate hike fell to 67%, from roughly 80% earlier in the week. 

AMERICAN SESSION

In the American session, we get the US NFP report, the Canadian employment data and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey. The NFP is expected at 65K vs 29K, with the unemployment rate remaining unchanged at 4.2%. The Average Hourly Earnings Y/Y is expected at 2.9% vs 3.0% prior, while the M/M measure is seen at 0.3% vs 0.1% prior. 

The reaction to data is going to be tricky because there could be something for everyone. A bad report could strengthen growth concerns and extend the risk-off sentiment. At the same time, it could also lead to a dovish repricing in interest rate expectations and support risk assets on a less hawkish Fed. In the current context, I would say the former is more probable.

The same goes for a good report. In this case, we might see a hawkish repricing that could weigh further on risk assets. But, good data could also trigger a relief rally on easing growth concerns. I guess the market would like to see good data, just not too hot. 

The Canadian employment change is expected at 13.6K vs -68.3K prior, with the unemployment rate remaining unchanged at 6.8%. The market is pricing just a 38% chance of a BoC rate hike in December, so we will likely need a very strong report followed by hot inflation data to raise the probabilities. I personally think the BoC shouldn't have hiked based on the data as labour market conditions has been soft and underlying inflation has held around the 2% target. A global rout in stock markets would just add downward pressure on economic activity. 

The University of Michigan consumer sentiment is expected at 48.0 vs 46.7 prior. We could see a minor rebound in the sentiment after the drop in gasoline prices, but I don't expect the data to matter much at this point.

item.title: Nasdaq analysis after yesterday's crash: Is this the dip investors have been waiting for?
item.description:
Nasdaq futures rebound after a 16.6% plunge. Is this a dip to buy or a rally to sell?

Nasdaq futures have bounced nearly 800 points from a major historical support zone, but Wall Street's earnings mood remains defensive. With another important economic report approaching, Friday could provide a crucial test of whether buyers are returning or the bearish trend is simply taking a break.

November 6, 2026 | Nasdaq-100 E-mini Futures (NQ)

Nasdaq-100 futures have fallen 5,250 points, or 16.61%, from their October high in just 23 trading sessions. Yet the latest decline has brought NQ into a particularly interesting support zone around 26,350-26,400, where buyers have finally responded.

Is this a dip worth buying? Possibly. But the price recovery, while impressive, remains unconfirmed, and the broader earnings environment gives me reasons to remain cautious.

The Nasdaq selloff has been brutal, but the latest low is interesting

Thursday's session delivered another reminder of how quickly market sentiment can change.

The cash Nasdaq-100 index declined 6.36%, its worst single-day performance since 2020, with selling particularly severe across artificial intelligence, semiconductors and data-center infrastructure companies.

As investingLive reported in its review of the Nasdaq-100 selloff, the pressure extended well beyond a handful of high-profile technology stocks.

The decline was also visible in the broader market. European trading saw US technology and chip liquidation intensify, although European equity markets themselves delivered a more mixed performance.

But while the headlines describe a market under considerable pressure, the futures chart offers another perspective.

From an October high of 31,616.50, Nasdaq futures have declined to 26,366.50 in the latest overnight session.

That is a decline of exactly 5,250 points, or approximately 16.61%.

And the location of that low matters.

Why 26,350-26,400 is more than just another support level

The longer-term futures chart identifies two previous major highs:

  • 26,399: An important historical high.

  • 26,349: Another major historical high.

  • 26,366.50: The latest low reached during the selloff.

These three prices are clustered within just 50 points of each other.

When markets break above previous highs, those former resistance areas can sometimes become support during subsequent corrections.

The logic is straightforward: a price area where sellers previously stopped an advance may later attract buying when the market returns from above.

That does not always happen, of course.

But in this case, the response has been encouraging. Nasdaq futures rebounded to approximately 27,159, recovering nearly 793 points from their latest low.

For traders watching for signs of a possible bottom, this is an important development.

Still, I would distinguish between a successful initial defense of support and a confirmed reversal of the wider downtrend.

The futures market has recovered only about 15% of the preceding 5,250-point decline. There is still considerable technical damage to repair.

Earnings season offers another warning: Investors are becoming selective

I also think we should look beyond the Nasdaq chart to understand what may happen next.

The latest earnings season has been notably defensive.

In a provisional review of 337 companies with usable earnings-reaction data through November 5, approximately 35.3% recorded positive reactions. The equal-weighted average reaction was around -3.59%, compared with approximately -1.23% on a market-capitalization-weighted basis.

These are preliminary estimates based on mixed-source observations, not a complete census of final earnings returns. Nevertheless, the imbalance is worth monitoring.

It suggests that investors have been more inclined to punish disappointing reports than to reward companies broadly.

But the most recent earnings announcements also reveal an interesting exception.

In the latest available after-hours observations:

  • Airbnb (ABNB): Up approximately 11.0% following earnings.

  • Cloudflare (NET): Up approximately 14.1%.

  • DraftKings (DKNG): Down approximately 21.7%.

  • Atlassian (TEAM): Down approximately 16.5%.

These are provisional extended-hours reactions measured against their respective pre-earnings regular-session references, not completed Friday returns.

What interests me here is the contrast.

Investors are clearly still willing to reward individual companies, sometimes quite aggressively. However, the differences between winners and losers remain extreme.

Earlier in the week, initial positive reactions in companies such as AMD and Arista Networks also struggled to retain their gains.

That creates an additional question for Friday: Will the latest earnings winners retain their gains when regular trading begins, or will renewed selling pressure overwhelm them?

For Nasdaq traders, this matters because a more sustainable index rebound would be more convincing if it were accompanied by improving technology-sector participation and stronger follow-through after earnings.

These individual earnings reactions are evidence of market selectivity, not a calculation of their contribution to NQ futures.

The AI trade is also facing a different question

The market is reconsidering the economics of the enormous AI infrastructure buildout.

Interestingly, as Adam Button discussed in why markets might welcome a slower data-center expansion, reduced capital spending could actually benefit some of the largest technology platforms by improving free cash flow.

That creates an important distinction between companies spending heavily on AI infrastructure and those supplying the chips, equipment, power and construction capacity.

A slower buildout might help the finances of some hyperscalers while hurting demand expectations for some of their suppliers.

The market is not necessarily abandoning AI. It may be questioning the timing, scale and financial returns of the investment cycle.

For Nasdaq investors, this distinction could become increasingly important over the coming months.

Friday's Nasdaq tradeCompass: Two important activation levels

Turning back to the futures chart, my directional assessment remains -5 on a scale from -10 to +10, reflecting a bearish broader structure despite the developing rebound.

However, that assessment is not a prediction that Friday must be a negative session.

The following tradeCompass scenarios provide conditional reference points based on the latest available 30-minute futures chart.

Bullish scenario: Above 27,200

Buyers have encountered resistance around 27,135-27,160 during the latest recovery.

I would prefer to see NQ establish sustained trading above 27,200 before treating the rebound as a stronger intraday bullish opportunity.

A brief move through the level would not necessarily be sufficient. Ideally, buyers would demonstrate that they can hold recovered ground when sellers return.

Potential bullish partial profit targets:

The second target is particularly interesting because it is positioned just beneath a previous value-area resistance boundary around 27,488.50.

A successful recovery above this region would represent a more meaningful improvement in the short-term technical structure.

Conversely, if NQ breaks above 27,200 but quickly returns below the nearby recovery area, the bullish scenario would lose credibility.

Importantly, a recovery toward these targets would still not automatically confirm that the larger correction has ended.

Bearish scenario: Below 26,850

The bearish scenario becomes more attractive if sellers regain control and NQ establishes sustained trading below 26,850.

That would indicate a deterioration in the recovery structure and a loss of the nearby support concentration around 26,880.

Potential bearish partial profit targets:

TP4 is conditional on a decisive breakdown below the 26,350-26,400 historical support zone.

This distinction matters.

The area around 26,350-26,400 has already attracted meaningful buying interest. I would not assume that sellers can simply push through it without another contest.

The third bearish target, at 26,415, is therefore positioned ahead of that historical support region.

A sustained recovery above 27,200 would weaken the immediate bearish-reversal thesis and call for reassessment.

What about the area between 26,850 and 27,200?

For me, this is primarily a decision zone.

Nasdaq futures can remain inside this region without generating a sufficiently strong directional opportunity.

One alternative worth monitoring is a recovery toward 27,135-27,200 that fails to hold.

Such a rejection might provide a more attractive location for traders looking to sell a rally rather than chase the market lower after an already substantial decline.

But there must be evidence of rejection. Reaching resistance alone does not establish a short trade.

Equally, a trader considering a long should not assume that simply bouncing off historical support guarantees another advance.

Friday's US jobs report could change the picture quickly

There is another important consideration for November 6.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics employment report for October is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, one hour before the US stock market opens.

That could have an important influence on Nasdaq futures.

A report that materially changes expectations for Federal Reserve policy, inflation or economic growth could produce substantial volatility.

For example, weaker employment data might encourage expectations of easier monetary policy, but an unexpectedly severe deterioration could simultaneously raise concerns about future corporate earnings.

Likewise, stronger employment figures might support confidence in economic growth while potentially making interest-rate relief less likely.

The market's interpretation, not simply whether the number is above or below expectations, will matter.

That makes it especially important to reassess the futures map if the announcement produces a substantial price adjustment.

Meanwhile, political and geopolitical uncertainty remains another source of potential market volatility.

As Adam Button discussed in the market's search for signals from Donald Trump, investors are assessing whether the administration responds to the midterm election results by changing course or maintaining its existing approach to trade and foreign policy.

Energy markets add another dimension. The recent decline in refining margins and signs of potential normalization could eventually matter for fuel prices and inflation expectations, although significant energy-supply risks remain.

These developments should not automatically be treated as explanations for every Nasdaq price movement. They are additional variables that traders need to consider when interpreting the next move.

Is the Nasdaq dip an opportunity for longer-term investors?

I believe the 26,350-26,400 support cluster deserves attention beyond Friday's trading session.

For an investor looking to increase technology exposure after a substantial correction, a return to important historical price levels may offer an opportunity to evaluate potential entries.

But a lower price is not necessarily a better investment.

The latest earnings season illustrates why.

Some companies are experiencing considerable changes in their growth outlook, spending requirements and investor expectations. Others are still reporting results strong enough to attract substantial buying interest.

A longer-term investor should consider whether a company's earnings outlook, valuation and competitive position remain attractive, rather than relying exclusively on an index-level support zone.

For the Nasdaq as a whole, I would become more constructive if the historical support cluster continues to hold and the market begins establishing a sequence of higher lows and recovering important resistance areas.

If the cluster breaks decisively, however, the possibility of a deeper correction would require renewed consideration.

My Nasdaq outlook for Friday

There are two opposing developments worth respecting.

First, the broader technical structure remains bearish after a 16.61% correction. The weakness in earnings reactions, together with uncertainty surrounding the AI investment cycle, gives little reason to assume that the selling pressure has disappeared.

Second, Nasdaq futures have reached a historically meaningful support cluster and produced a substantial initial recovery.

That deserves attention too.

For Friday's day traders, 27,200 is the bullish activation level, while 26,850 is the bearish activation level.

For swing traders and investors, the more consequential reference remains 26,350-26,400.

I would be especially interested in whether buyers can sustain the recovery after the US employment report and into the regular trading session.

A successful defense, improving earnings follow-through and a recovery through successive resistance levels would strengthen the argument that the latest Nasdaq dip is becoming an opportunity.

A failed rebound, renewed selling across technology stocks and a decisive loss of historical support would argue otherwise.

My broader directional lean remains bearish, but the rebound has changed the short-term risk-reward picture. After such an extended decline, chasing shorts into major support deserves particular caution.

For traders using the tradeCompass approach, the objective remains to respond to evidence rather than predict every move. Consider partial profits at planned targets, size positions around a defined invalidation point and remember that doing nothing is sometimes the most sensible decision.

For more detail, see the investingLive guide to tradeCompass and its conditional trading approach.

Analysis based on the December 2026 Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures contract, with historical context from the continuous futures series. Price-data cutoff: November 5, 2026, 9:55 p.m. EST (November 6, 02:55 UTC). Overnight earnings reactions are provisional. Levels should be checked against the contract being traded.

Educational only. Futures trading involves substantial risk. Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

Wednesday’s rotation out of AI and into the broader market turned into a broad selloff on Thursday. The Nasdaq 100 took the biggest hit, but the Russell 2000 fell 4.45% and the Dow lost more than it gained the day before. Falling Treasury yields helped gold catch a bid. Crude went the other way. After Wednesday’s plunge on hopes for an end to the Iran war, reports of fresh Gulf shipping incidents put the risk to supplies back in focus. The dollar was mixed, with the Australian dollar taking the biggest hit among the majors and the yen holding up best.

The dollar gains against the Aussie but loses ground to the yen

AI suppliers lead the selloff

Europe closes mixed

InvestingLive’s European close

U.S. data hold up as markets look to Washington

InvestingLive’s Washington coverage

Crude rebounds as Gulf shipping risks resurface

item.title: Nasdaq 100 suffers worst day since 2020
item.description:
The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36% on Thursday, its worst day since 2020, as investors sold everything from memory and storage stocks to chip equipment makers and data-center suppliers. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, the S&P 500 dropped 4.35%, and the Dow lost 1,833 points. All three had their worst day since April 2025.

A day after the Dow surged nearly 1,600 points, it gave back the entire gain and then some. The Russell 2000 fell 4.45%, and all 30 Dow stocks closed lower. The selling was most intense in the AI trade, but by the close it had spread well beyond it.

Investors continued to weigh what the midterm results could mean for the pace of the AI data-center buildout. Treasury yields moved lower and gold caught a bid as stocks sold off. Lower yields can help growth stocks, but today they came alongside a broad move away from risk and offered little relief to tech.

U.S. stock market closing levels

  • Dow Jones Industrial Average −1,833.16 points (−3.44%) to 51,528.16

  • S&P 500 −334.77 points (−4.35%) to 7,353.85

  • Nasdaq Composite −1,421.52 points (−5.52%) to 24,315.00

  • Russell 2000 −127.11 points (−4.45%) to 2,729.84

  • Nasdaq 100 −1,807.36 points (−6.36%) to 26,629.81

Every Dow stock fell

Nvidia led the Dow lower with a 9.26% decline. Cisco fell 7.62%, Goldman Sachs lost 6.44%, Caterpillar dropped 6.39%, and Honeywell fell 5.55%. Verizon (−0.04%) and Coca-Cola (−0.07%) came closest to finishing flat.

The breadth numbers tell the same story. S&P 500 decliners outnumbered advancers 411 to 75. Across the Nasdaq, 2,822 stocks fell and 463 rose, a little more than six decliners for every advancer. On the NYSE Composite, the count was 1,512 down and 288 up.

The AI and chip names that fell 10% or more

The closing watchlist showed 22 individual stocks down at least 10%, plus the VanEck Semiconductor ETF. Sandisk led the declines, and the losses ran through nearly every part of the chip and data-center supply chain.

  • Memory and storage — Sandisk −22.26%, Micron Technology −17.46%, Western Digital −17.35%.

  • Chip designers and manufacturers — AMD −17.26%, Arm Holdings −13.08%, Taiwan Semiconductor −10.78%, Texas Instruments −10.70%, Broadcom −10.43%, Intel −10.33%, Monolithic Power Systems −10.28%.

  • Networking, connectivity and optics — Astera Labs −19.62%, Lumentum −18.68%, Credo Technology −17.71%, Marvell Technology −16.43%, Coherent −12.98%, Arista Networks −10.82%.

  • Semiconductor equipment and components — Lam Research −16.36%, Applied Materials −13.58%, SkyWater Technology −13.40%, KLA −13.35%.

  • Data-center compute and power — Nebius Group −14.95%, Bloom Energy −16.41%.

  • Semiconductor ETF — VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) −11.21%.

All seven Mag 7 stocks fall, led by Tesla and Nvidia

There was no green in the Magnificent Seven, but there was a big difference in how the stocks held up. Tesla fell 10.77% and Nvidia lost 9.26%. They were the only two to fall more than the S&P 500 (−4.35%), the Nasdaq Composite (−5.52%) and the Nasdaq 100 (−6.36%).

Apple held up best, down 1.53%, followed by Amazon (−2.19%) and Alphabet (−2.20%). Microsoft and Meta also held up better than the three broader indices, although both fell more than the Dow (−3.44%).

  • Tesla −10.77% to $343.69

  • Nvidia −9.26% to $181.60

  • Meta Platforms −3.96% to $605.08

  • Microsoft −3.58% to $535.93

  • Alphabet −2.20% to $282.57

  • Amazon −2.19% to $260.21

  • Apple −1.53% to $344.17

On the next bounce, I’ll be watching Tesla and Nvidia. If buyers step in and those two can hold their gains, it would be an early sign that the selling pressure is easing in the hardest-hit megacaps.

The YTD scorecard after the selloff

The YTD numbers put the selloff in perspective. SanDisk fell more than 20% on the day and was still up more than 200% for the year. Micron and AMD each fell about 17%, yet both held on to substantial YTD gains. Nvidia and Broadcom were already on the other side of the ledger by the end of the session. The selling hit the chip stocks hard, but the cushion going into the day varied considerably.

The Magnificent 7 are split three up and four down. Apple leads the group at roughly +27% YTD, with Amazon and Microsoft still up double digits. Tesla is the weakest at about −24%. Outside tech, Target, Chevron, ExxonMobil and Coca-Cola are still sitting on sizable gains. Meanwhile, some of the deepest losses on the watchlist are in software, with Intuit down about 46% and Oracle off 41%.

All five major U.S. indices are still positive for 2026 after the November 5 selloff. The Russell 2000 is the only one still up double digits, while the Nasdaq Composite has the smallest gain. AP News

Price returns through the November 5 close, measured from the December 31, 2025 close.

The Nasdaq Composite went into the session up about 10.7% for the year and came out up just 4.6%. The S&P 500’s gain narrowed from about 12.3% to 7.4%.

What traders should watch after a selloff like this

Sellers have control heading into the next session. The first thing I’ll watch on a bounce is whether it can hold and whether more stocks participate. A few megacaps can lift an index early even while most stocks are still falling. If breadth improves and the chip stocks that led the decline start to hold their rebounds, buyers have more evidence that the selling is easing. If those stocks give back their gains and breadth stays weak, the burden remains on the buyers.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Magnificent 7: What are the technicals telling traders for each of those companies him
item.description:
In the video above, I take a look at the Magnificent 7 as the broader U.S. indices sell off sharply. The S&P 500 is down around 4%, the Nasdaq Composite is down 5.10%, and the Nasdaq 100 is down 5.75%. All seven stocks are lower, but only two are falling more than all three indices. Those two are Nvidia and Tesla.

Apple and Alphabet hold up best

Apple leads the group with a decline of 1.27%, followed by Alphabet, down 1.53%. Amazon is down 2.49%, Microsoft is lower by 3.64%, and Meta is down 3.87%. All five are outperforming both Nasdaq indices, although Apple and Alphabet are doing so by a much wider margin than Microsoft and Meta.

For Apple and Alphabet, the question is whether that relative strength shows up at support. Can buyers lean against a level and put in a low? If they can, the next test is whether the price can get back above the first resistance level and stay there. That would give buyers something to build on.

Nvidia and Tesla see the most selling

Nvidia is down 8.55%, while Tesla is the weakest of the seven with a decline of 11.19%. Both are falling considerably more than the Nasdaq 100. For those two, I’m watching what happens on a bounce. If sellers lean against a broken support level on the way back up, that old floor becomes a ceiling and keeps the downside bias intact. If the price gets back above that level and holds, sellers have lost some of their control.

The levels that matter from here

On a day like this, the size of the decline tells you where the pressure is. The technical levels give you a way to judge whether that pressure is easing or building. Does the price break support and stay below it, opening the door to the next downside target? Or does it dip below, snap back above, and force sellers to rethink the break?

That distinction also helps define risk. If buyers lean against support, they have a nearby level that tells them when the trade is going against them. If sellers lean against resistance on a bounce, they have the same kind of barometer on the topside.

Watch the video above for the key levels in all seven stocks, where buyers or sellers can lean, and what would shift the bias from here.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: WTI crude oil settles at $90.52, up 2.72% as buyers defend key support
item.description:
U.S. crude oil futures settled at $90.52 a barrel on Thursday, up $2.40 or 2.72% from Wednesday’s $88.12 settlement. The rebound follows a drop of more than 8% on Wednesday, when the U.S. midterm results raised hopes that a Democratic-controlled Congress would increase pressure on the Trump administration to end the war with Iran.

Gulf shipping risk is back in focus

On Wednesday, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats would seek to end the war, pointing to Congress’s control over spending. By Thursday, traders were again weighing the risk to oil shipments. Reuters reported that at least five vessels had reported incidents in the Gulf since Sunday, citing UK Maritime Trade Operations. Iran’s foreign minister also spoke with his Saudi and Qatari counterparts about diplomatic efforts. The prospect of de-escalation helped take some risk premium out of oil on Wednesday. The shipping reports gave traders a reason to put some of it back in on Thursday.

Wednesday’s U.S. inventory report also showed draws in crude, gasoline and distillates for the week ended October 30. The draws offered some support heading into Thursday’s session.

Buyers defended $86.65–$86.93. Can they get above $91.56?

On the WTI chart, the selloff reached $86.65, right near the 200-day moving average at the time. The 100-day moving average was between that low and the 50% midpoint of the rally from the July low at $86.93. That gave buyers a well-defined area to lean against, and they did.

The next test is $91.56, the broken 38.2% retracement of that same rally. The futures settlement was $1.04 below it. Move above $91.56 and stay above, and buyers would have more room to retrace Wednesday’s selloff. Stall there and sellers have a level to lean against. A break back below $86.65–$86.93 would put the 61.8% retracement at $82.30 in play.

Trading takeaway

A bounce off support tells you where buyers were willing to step in. The next clue comes at former support. If buyers can reclaim $91.56 and hold it on a pullback, they’ll have a closer level to define their risk. If sellers defend it, the bounce remains vulnerable to a retest of the lows.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The market is waiting for signals from Donald Trump
item.description:
I spoke to Reuters earlier today about the state of markets and my comments boiled down to this:

"There are two ​paths Trump can go down - he can double down on unpopular trade ​wars or he can listen to the electorate and change course," said Adam Button, chief currency analyst at investingLive.

That's the crossroads we are at right now and I think it shows some of the tension in markets.

An early sign we got was on replacing Pete Hegseth:

“No, I think he’s doing a very good job.”

Of course, Trump has said that many times before replacing staff, so I wouldn't take it as the final word. It's worth noting though that George H. W. Bush fired Donald Rumsfeld the day after the 2006 midterms, in large part due to the unpopular Iran war.

Trump did also tease at Hegseth taking the Tennessee Senate seat after its senator won the Governorship, soemthing he could in January.

Alternatively, House member Thomas Massie has pledge to start impeach Hegseth, and there's ample evidence that they could get the votes to do it, either before or after the new Congress is sworn in. Many Senators will be looking to reframe their anti-war, America First chops and Hegseth is a convenient scapegoat.

At the same time, there is a big distinction in how he's removed. If it's from Trump, it will be a sign that he's sick of the Iran war and will end it. If it's Congress, that still leaves a pro-war President in power.

In terms of the timeline, earlier NYT reporting about three aircraft carriers in the Gulf was incorrect. The USS Roosevelt will arrive in the Gulf in mid-November and that could be the window for strikes. There is talk the USS George Washington needs to depart the area soon so there is only a short overlap.

There is a similar dynamic unfolding around tariffs. Congress has lost patience with USMCA tariffs and perhaps some others. Expect some action on that either in the lame duck session or early next year.

Again, Trump has the option of cutting a deal beforehand and there's talk deals are close with Canada and Mexico. If he does that, it could bring down the temperature but Congress may still want to go further and repeal some tariffs to show they're fighting to bring down the cost of living.

One thing that worries me is that Trump reposted this message:

If he decides to double down on his worst instincts, it will keep inflation high, make the Fed's job harder and likely lead the market to price in even more Democrat gains in 2028.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Europe Close: AI and chip liquidation drags equities lower in US, but Europe is mixed.
item.description:
As London and European traders head home, the main story is the liquidation in US stocks. AI and chip names are taking the hardest hit as investors weigh the path forward after the US midterm elections. Yesterday, the Dow surged nearly 1,600 points even as parts of the AI trade struggled. Today, the Dow has given back most of that gain, the Russell 2000 is down more than 4%, and the Nasdaq 100 is down more than 5%. The Nasdaq indices have bounced off their lows, but the Dow and Russell are still right on theirs. European stocks finish mixed as the BOE hikes

item.title: AUDUSD sellers have pushed to the lowest level since mid-October. What next?
item.description:
Sellers have been leaning against retracement levels.

Going back to last week, the rally in the AUDUSD stalled near 0.7065, the 50% retracement of the move down from the September 9 high. Staying below, kept the seller in play. 

This week - on Monday - the pair set its high for the week as it tested the 100-hour and 100-day moving averages (blue lines on the chart below), both near 0.7030 at the time. The 38.2% retracement of the same move was just below at 0.7025.

The price moved below those levels and reached 0.6954 yesterday before snapping back higher as US stocks rallied and the market shifted back toward risk-on after the US elections. That bounce took the pair back toward 0.7025, where sellers leaned against the broken 38.2% retracement today.

The stock selloff took the AUDUSD to a fresh low.

As US stocks sold off today, so did the AUDUSD. The pair fell below the 200-hour moving average at 0.70159, the 100-hour moving average at 0.7003, and the swing area between 0.6989 and 0.6994. The selling picked up as the stock indices extended their declines. The pair broke yesterday’s 0.6954 low and traded down to 0.6949, its lowest level since October 19.

What now?

The close barometer for buyers and sellers is 0.6970–0.6977. That area represents the 38.2% to 50% retracement of the North American session’s trend move down from 0.7006 (see 5-minute chart) him. If buyers can’t get back above that zone, the path of least resistance remains to the downside, with the next support at 0.6932–0.6936. There are a number of prior swing lows and highs in that area, so watch how the price reacts on a test.

If buyers can get above 0.6977 and stay above it, the sellers lose some of their grip. That would put the broken 0.6989–0.6994 swing area back in play. Buyers would need to reclaim that area to build on a bounce, with the 100-hour moving average at 0.7003 the next hurdle.

Trading education. Match the retracement to the move you’re trading.

There are two different 38.2% retracements in this setup. The one at 0.7025 measures the broader move down from the September 9 high and helps explain where sellers showed up today. The one near 0.6970 measures the much shorter drop from 0.7006 and gives traders a closer level to judge the strength of the next bounce.

How much of the drop can buyers take back? If a bounce stalls near 0.6970, sellers are still keeping the correction shallow. If buyers get above the 50% midpoint near 0.6977 and hold it, they’ve taken back more than half of the session’s drop. That’s a reason for sellers to reassess their close risk. The next test is whether buyers can turn the former floor at 0.6989–0.6994 back into support.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Oil cracks are beginning to fall and refineries are pointing to more normalization
item.description:
The price of oil at $89 isn't that big of a problem for consumers or businesses. Crude has come down dramatically this week and a big part of that is expectations that Trump or Congress will find a way to open Hormuz and end the Iran war.

That remains to be seen but what hasn't changed is ultra-wide crack spreads. Normalized gasoline would be selling around $3.60-3.75 right now with diesel slightly higher with cracks around $22 (gasoline) and $30 (diesel). Because of all the refining tightness, gasoline has about a 60-cent premium and diesel at about +$2.25.

That's proven to be a big problem electorally and won't get better so long as the wars in Ukraine and Iran continue. If anything, they will worsen in time on potentially escalated strikes from Ukraine, Iran, the USA and Houthis.

From the looks of it, the prognosis is bad and winter sees higher distillate demand as well for heating. 

There is a positive sign though, the share prices of refineries are rolling over. Valero is a pure play and it's down 22% since October 13.

More broadly, the CRAK refiners ETF is down 16% from the October peak. 

In mid-October, the product tightness was extreme with $100 cracks. That's narrowed to $77 in jet fuel and even more in distillates. Diesel cracks are at $83 coimpared to $102 in mid-October and $92 on October 23. Notably, cracks haven't come in further in the past few days but refiners continue to fall. That could be a forward-looking indicator or market beta but it's worth watching. 

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin falls with risk off sentiment. The price is testing a key swing area target.
item.description:
Recall that Bitcoin moved higher with stocks on Wednesday, pushing back above $79,146 and into the old swing area that extends to $81,930. The move gave buyers a shot at taking back more control. To do that, they needed to get through the top of the area and stay above it. The rally stalled within the zone, and the price has since fallen back below $79,146.

Thursday. The risk-off crowd takes over

With the Nasdaq and chip stocks under pressure, Bitcoin has given back the rebound and moved back below its 100-day moving average at $76,950. The price was near $76,600 in the chart snapshot after testing the upper edge of the $74,925–$76,052 swing area. The 38.2% retracement of the summer rally comes in at $76,052, making that level the first downside barometer.

What next? The swing floor is the bigger test

For sellers, the 100-day MA at $76,950 is the close risk level. Stay below it, and the sellers keep the short-term advantage. Get below $76,052 and stay below, and the focus shifts to the swing-area floor at $74,925. A sustained break of that floor would open the door toward the 200-day MA at $73,195 and then the 50% retracement at $72,554.

For buyers, the first job is to hold the swing area and get back above $76,950. If they can get above that moving average and stay above it, the 100- and 200-hour MAs at $78,152 and $78,373 are the next targets. Above those, $79,146 comes back into focus.

In the video above, I talk about the technicals in more detail and explain the bias, the risks and targets.  

Education. How to lean against a swing area

A swing area gives traders a range where price has repeatedly changed direction. Here, $76,052 is the first level buyers can lean against, while $74,925 is the floor that defines the broader support area. If price breaks below $76,052 and quickly gets back above it, sellers who chased the break may have to cover. Getting above the 100 day MA would be a risk and bias defining confirmation level that if broken, would give buyers more confidence. If price stays below $76,052, the lower end of the range becomes the next test. That distinction lets traders define their risk before they enter and judge the trade by what price does at the level.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The market is telling the hyperscalers it's happy about a slower data center buildout
item.description:
Perhaps the clearest takeaway from Tuesday's US midterms is that data centers are unpopular. After a short-lived construction boom, they provide little ongoing employment and drive up local energy costs. There were 41 local votes on data center curbs and 40 of them are on track to win, with margins in the 75/25% range.

Microsoft and Amazon are heavily into the data center business, including huge plans to build more so they should be losers today, right? Wrong. Shares of those two are up around 7% and the market cheers a slower, smaller data center buildout. The market has been hating the massive spending on highly-inflated chips and data center supply chains.

In effect, the market is saying that the government is doing for you what you should be doing. Now the companies themselves have been trying to sell Wall Street on data center economics but the cash demands are simply too high and the market has said that the risk-reward isn't convincing. 

At this point, there might be some reflexivity in company management. Now that they've seen how the stock reacts to data center curbs, they might slow their own ambitions to levels closer to matching free cash flow. If so, that could be a powerful tailwind for the stocks, which have struggled this year.

Amazon is particularly compelling as its core business of goods delivery isn't under threat from AI in the same way as a software company like Microsoft. 

The flipside is that the companies in the data center building business are struggling. The neoclouds and vendors are all down big today, along with the companies that would be contract to provide the power to the data centers. 

Forthe next moves, watch what kind of agenda congressional Democrats set around AI and data centers. They have a wide menu of things to choose to go after, including rampant corruption. I tend to think that some level of oversight around AI is coming but I'm not sure they want to take on data centers at the national level. 

Another spot to watch is in Texas and Ohio, where more than one-quarter of planned data center capacity is located. Both of the new Democratic governors campaigned against data centers and it will be critical to see how they plan to act.

Most important those are voters, who have clearly showed they don't want to pay higher electricity rates so OpenAI can run the data centers harder.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Memory names getting smoked: Micron breaks the July low in 12% drop
item.description:
Shares of Micron have taken an ugly turn today, dropping 12% and breaking support at the July low.

Chip stocks are down heavily as the market re-thinks the pace of the AI build out. There are a few reasons for the change in thinking:

  1. The election showed US voters are heavily against data centers, with 40 of 41 direct votes on them failing and many candidates who were pro-data center losing
  2. The market initially rewarded the hyperscalers for those votes, showing that stock prices will improve if they slow spending
  3. Various reports show it will be impossible to power the pace of building data centers
  4. If data centers can be built, public opposition will result in higher costs because companies will have to pledge to build all the power infrastructure to go with them, essentially moving them off grid

The flip side of the argument is that Micron is making tremendous amounts of money right now and the order book is deep. The actual result for FY26 was $74.33 per shares, and that puts it at 9.3x this year's earnings. Moreover, the consensus rises to $177 for the fiscal year that just started so just 4x earnings. The consensus rises to $212 for 2028 but I wouldn't weigh that too heavily.

For what it's worth, the company has said the industry will be more supply-constrained in both 2027 and 2028 than in 2026. For HBM, they said a large portion of output is sold. Micron also said at the end of the quarter that more than 75% of production is committed.

Notably, Micron is trying to diminish its traditional cyclicality. It has signed 26 strategic customer agreements, expected to cover more than 35% of cumulative revenue through 2030. Approximately 75% of that revenue has defined pricing arrangements, primarily floors and ceilings. These agreements are multiyear take-or-pay contracts.

Despite that, there is some major variance in analyst revenue estimtes for the next two years.

The next thing to watch is the chart, it's ugly. Today's break of the July low cuts through support and puts it back at May levels.

Another data center buildout darling -- Caterpillar -- has already turned negative on the year after rising 86% YTD in late June. The market could be seeing technical changes coming from advanced models that need less memory, or this could be about the buildout.

Another possibility -- which I put a high weight on -- is that this is an irrational, emotional market. It's filled with fast-money options traders that trade on momentum. There is little thought given to earnings except on earnings data. After that, it's all an AI sentiment trade and right now there is an ebb in AI sentiment.

That said, I do think those earnings numbers are grounded in reality and it's hard to see a total cliff before 2029. That should make something like 3x next year's earnings akin to an absolute floor and that's around $530. There is also some support at $661, which was the mid-May low. 

Micron's next earnings report is likely to be in mid-to-late December.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Crude oil tests the key confluence area and finds willing buyers
item.description:
Crude oil futures fell sharply yesterday as traders weighed the chances of an end to the war with Iran. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats would push to end the war and pointed to support from some Republicans. Crude was down close to 8% when I wrote about the move.

The headlines helped drive the selloff. The technicals gave traders a place to lean against. Yesterday, I highlighted three levels within 27 cents of one another. The 50% midpoint of the move up from the July low came in at $86.93, the 100-day MA at $86.81 and the 200-day MA at $86.66. A move below that area that could stay below would give sellers room to roam. A hold would give buyers a shot at a bounce. Yesterday’s crude oil analysis

Today’s low reached $86.65, a penny below the 200-day MA, and bounced. Crude is trading at $89.26, up $1.17, or about 1.3%, after reaching a high of $90.35.

What do buyers need to get above?

After a sharp move like yesterday’s, I like to measure the last trend leg to see how much of it buyers can take back. On the 5-minute chart, measuring from yesterday’s high to today’s low puts the 38.2% retracement at $90.68. Today’s high of $90.35 fell 33 cents short. As long as the price stays below $90.68, the sellers still have the upper hand on that trend leg.

Get above $90.68 and stay above, and the focus shifts to $91.56, the broken 38.2% retracement of the broader rally from the early July low. Reclaiming that level would give buyers another reason to press toward $91.92, the 50% midpoint of the latest selloff. Taking back half of that decline would give buyers more control in the short term.

Where is the risk for buyers?

On a move lower, watch the 100- and 200-bar MAs on the 5-minute chart. A sustained move below both would tilt the short-term bias back toward the sellers and bring the $86.66–$86.93 support area back into focus. If sellers can get below today’s $86.65 low and stay below it, they’ll have done what they couldn’t do on the first test.

Trading lesson — How much of the selloff can buyers take back?

After a sharp selloff, I look for two clues. First, where do buyers show up? Second, how much of the decline can they take back? In crude oil, the first clue came at $86.65, where the price tested the 200-day MA and bounced. The second clue comes at $90.68, the 38.2% retracement of the last leg lower.

I use 38.2% as a minimum retracement when judging whether buyers are starting to take back control. If the bounce stalls below that level, sellers still have the advantage on that leg. If the price gets above it and holds, especially on a retest, buyers have a nearby level to lean against. That gives them a way to define their risk while looking for the next target.

There are two 38.2% levels in this setup because they measure two different moves. $90.68 measures how much of the latest selloff buyers have taken back. $91.56 measures the pullback of the broader rally from July and marks a level crude broke on the way down. Clearing the first would strengthen the bounce. Reclaiming the second would show buyers starting to repair some of the damage on the hourly chart.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Marco Rubio ‘on resignation watch’ - report
item.description:
The Independent reports that Marco Rubio "is on resignation watch from both sides of the Atlantic in the expectation he will quit to lauch a bid to be the next US President".

The report cites "senior party sources in the US and senior figures in the UK government" and notes that he was plotting his exit even before the disasterous midterms. 

Rival JD Vance already distanced himself from Trump by tring to take an anti-war stance and blaming the Iran war for the Republicans loss. It may be tough for him and Rubio to cast themselves as opponents to war after defending it in the first 9 months of fighting.

The Independent said up to five members of Trump's cabinet are considering runs for President. As for Rubio, a source said he needs “distance himself from the Iran war and pin that one on Trump.”

I had thought that Rubio would stick around as Secretary of State for a longer period because Cuba has been his longstanding issue and the US appers to be plotting regime change their. Rubio's family immigrated from Cuba prior to Fidel Castro's revolution.

In betting markets, the odds for Ron DeSantis have improved dramatically this week as he launches critcisms of the administration as an outsider.

This is the nature of politics and now that the Iran war is seen as a failure, none of them will want to take responsibility for it. Meanwhile, none of them resigned in February when the war started, so Vance and Rubio will be vulnerable to attacks from other candidates who say they were never the "America First" politicians they said they were.

At the same time, if any of them distance themselves too far from Trump, he will turn thin-skinned and sabotage their candidacies. That set-up may make it easier for outsiders to take leadership of the party.

However given the results of the primaries, the real battle to get a Republican president in the next election may come down to policymaking in the next two years. If tariffs, inflation and the Iran war are still going on in 2028, it's tough to imagine any of them having a real chance, given the results on Tuesday.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: US initial jobless claims 189K vs 196K estimate
item.description:
• Prior week initial claims 194K
  • Prior week continuing claims 1.701M

Details

  • Initial jobless claims (October 31) fell 6,000 to 189,000. Prior revised to 195,000 from 194,000.

  • Initial claims four-week average fell 2,250 to 194,750. Prior revised to 197,000 from 196,750.

  • Continuing claims (October 24) rose 23,000 to 1,718,000. Prior revised to 1,695,000 from 1,701,000.

  • Continuing claims four-week average rose 1,000 to 1,709,500. Prior revised to 1,708,500 from 1,710,000.

  • Insured unemployment rate (October 24) held at 1.1%.

U.S. initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 in the week ending October 31, the Labor Department reported. The four-week average also fell, pointing to fewer new filings even after smoothing out some of the weekly noise.

Continuing claims moved the other way, rising to 1.718 million in the week ending October 24. The four-week average edged up by just 1,000, so the rise was more pronounced in the weekly figure than in the recent trend.

Quick analysis

The drop in initial claims points to limited layoff pressure. On its own, that gives the Fed less reason to hurry toward a rate cut and can lend some support to the dollar and short-term Treasury yields. The rise in continuing claims tempers that signal because it can point to people taking longer to find work. The next few readings will show whether that rise is becoming a trend.

What this report measures

Initial claims count new filings for unemployment benefits and give traders an early read on layoffs. Continuing claims track ongoing filings and are reported with an extra week’s lag. Both headline figures are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision, and traders watch their four-week averages to gauge the labor-market trend.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.
